text: Harbour City’s patient, short-passing buildup over 17 passes and nearly a minute demonstrated excellent possession control and tactical discipline, aligning well with Tomasz Rhee’s 4-2-3-1 approach. The team effectively exploited the central gap left by Seabrook Town’s wide-oriented 3-4-3 defense, culminating in Marek Barros’s incisive through ball to Elias Okafor, who converted from 13.9 meters. Seabrook’s defensive shape struggled to cover the central corridor, a vulnerability Harbour City used to break the deadlock just before halftime. Going forward, emphasize maintaining composure in tight central spaces to exploit similar structural weaknesses in opponents' defense.
